title: The Last Uniform
premise: In 1914 London, Rafael Marchetti, an Italian immigrant who drives for suffragist Edith Calloway and secretly reads the letters he delivers, is handed a six-year-old girl, Lucia, by an Austrian governess fleeing internment — with orders to forget her face. The child carries a coded inheritance: her late father's shares in a shipping firm that profited from both sides of the coming war, and proof that Edith's own brother helped forge the will that disinherited Lucia. Rafael must choose between the found family he serves and justice for a child declared enemy, smuggling Lucia and the documents to her surviving aunt in Liverpool before the Home Office's alien-registration sweep reaches them. He succeeds at the cost of his position and nearly his freedom, but Edith, confronted with her brother's crime, chooses principle over blood and helps him escape — ending with Rafael and Lucia on a northbound train, a new family built from a broken promise kept.
about_author: Ines Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing internee letters from the First World War. She writes historical fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Establishes his ritual of reading letters before delivery, his careful invisibility as an Italian driver in suspicious wartime London, and his quiet devotion to Edith Calloway. When war is declared, household staff scatter and orders come to dismiss 'enemy' servants. Emotional beat: a man who measures safety in suitcases realizes his own are already packed.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A rain-soaked night: the Austrian governess Anna leaves Lucia on the step with a sealed satchel and one instruction — forget my face. Inside the satchel: shares, a disputed will, and a letter naming Edith's brother Gerald as witness to a forgery. Emotional beat: terror transforming into reluctant guardianship when Lucia calls him 'the letter man.'

chapters.title: Enemy Property
chapters.summary: Alternating Rafael and Edith POVs. Rafael hides Lucia in the mews while Edith returns from a suffrage march to find her household under police observation. Gerald arrives demanding any papers the governess left. Emotional beat: Edith's loyalty to family colliding with instincts she can't yet name; Rafael lying fluently for the first time in his honest life.

chapters.title: The Reading of Letters
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Flashback woven through present: how years of reading Edith's correspondence taught him the shipping firm's secrets, including Gerald's debts. Now he decodes the father's letter using patterns learned from a thousand intercepted lives. Emotional beat: the reader of other people's words finally forced to write his own — a false travel pass for a child.

chapters.title: A Promise Made in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Anna's letter reveals the promise: she once hid Rafael's brother from Austrian police in Trieste, saving his life. The debt has come due across enemy lines. Meanwhile the registration sweep tightens; neighbors report 'foreign voices' in the mews. Emotional beat: gratitude outliving nations, and the weight of owing your life to someone now officially an enemy.

chapters.title: Gerald's Ledger
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. Edith discovers Gerald's forged-witness signature in the firm's records during a board dinner she attends as his guest. Confronted privately, he offers her money and warns that sheltering an enemy child makes her a traitor too. Emotional beat: the sickening clarity of seeing a beloved brother clearly for the first time.

chapters.title: The Sweep
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Police search the mews; Rafael smuggles Lucia out through the coal cellar into a suffragist safe-house network he once drove marchers through. A sympathetic constable looks away — justice outside the law wearing a uniform. Emotional beat: the hunted finding that the persecuted have always had their own maps.

chapters.title: Northbound
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Rafael and Lucia flee toward Liverpool by train, pursued by Gerald's hired man; Edith stays behind to destroy evidence and delay the warrant, finally choosing the child over the brother. A near-capture at Crewe station resolved by Lucia's quick lie. Emotional beat: fear braided with fierce tenderness; two orphans of different wars becoming family.

chapters.title: The Aunt in Liverpool
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The aunt, a dockside widow, receives Lucia and the documents; a solicitor agrees to contest the will, but only if Rafael testifies — exposing himself to deportation. Gerald's man corners Rafael at the docks; the constable from the sweep intervenes. Emotional beat: courage priced honestly, and the choice to pay it.

chapters.title: The Last Uniform
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, coda. Months later: the will overturned, Gerald discredited, Edith arrived unannounced in Liverpool having dismissed herself from her old life. Rafael, offered his position back, declines — he keeps the aunt's books instead, and Lucia's letters arrive openly now, read by everyone they're meant for. Emotional beat: a man who once carried everything learning to stay; a promise kept becoming a home.
